newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT-Dlr/mark close above 1.52 builds bull base.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT-Dlr/mark close above 1.52 builds bull base.

text.p: Despite an afternoon retreat from dollar/mark's 1.53 session high, technicians said on Tuesday that another close above 1.52 should keep the rate's bullish momentum intact.
"As long as we close above 1.52, I'm pretty favorable," said Pete Grant, senior foreign exchange analyst at MMS International.

Grant said the 1.5454 October high in dollar/mark is a legitimate near-term objective, but cautioned that strong resistance at Tuesday's 1.53 high and congestion at 1.5340/50 could make the climb arduous.

A second consecutive close above the 1.2850 level in dollar/Swiss should reinforce the bull run in dollar/mark, technicians argued. They said much depends on the ability of the dollar to move above 1.30 Swiss francs without falling victim to profit-taking.

"The real key support level that you want to see it hold above is 1.2850," said John Tirone, technical analyst at Chase Securities Inc, referring to dollar/Swiss. "I thought it was really positive that we closed above it last night and now the close you want to see is 1.2940."
In mid-afternoon trade dollar/Swiss stood at 1.2910/20.

In cable, which regained some ground on Tuesday after coming sharply off multi-year highs recently, chartists pegged key resistance at $1.6750/60. They said a return to sterling's recent high of $1.6905 remained distinctly in the cards.
Like dollar/mark, dollar/yen could also retest its October high of 114.92 if it can hurdle a near-term ceiling below 113.
"We think 112.89 to 113-the-figure is resistance ... and if we break above that I'm pretty optimistic about a retest of the late October highs," said MMS's Grant.
